story_title: As an Event Coordinator, I want to see every venue booking, equipment reservation and registration list that has been flagged for review across my events so that I can re-check each one and keep or replace it before it causes a problem

acceptance_criteria.text: The Event Coordinator can view a list of flagged venue bookings, equipment reservations and registrations for the events assigned to them.

Each flagged arrangement shows the event, the arrangement, and why it was flagged (e.g. event date changed, attendance changed, venue attributes updated, venue setup or turnaround time changed, venue retired, venue blocked, equipment marked unavailable).
Given an event has more than one venue booking, when one of them is flagged, then only the flagged booking is listed.
For a flagged venue booking, the current suitability and availability result for the event's present requirements is shown.
For a flagged equipment reservation, the current availability result for the event's present dates and quantities is shown.
Given the arrangement still meets the event's requirements, when the Coordinator keeps it, then the flag is cleared and the arrangement is unchanged.
Given the arrangement no longer meets the event's requirements, when the Coordinator attempts to keep it, then the flag is not cleared and the unmet requirement is identified.

For flagged registrations, the number of attendees registered or on the waiting list is shown, with why they were flagged: the event's date or time changed (see: Update Event Information, SPM-62), or the registration capacity was lowered below the number registered or registration was turned off (see: Configure Event Registration, SPM-64).
Given registrations are flagged, when the Coordinator marks them as reviewed, then the flag is cleared and no registration is changed.
Flagged registrations do not prevent confirmation.

From a flagged venue booking, the Coordinator can search for a replacement venue, with the search pre-filled from that booking's date, start and end times, attendance, layout, accessibility and facility requirements.
The Coordinator can request the replacement venue; the flagged booking stays on the event record until the Coordinator releases it (see: Withdraw or Release Venue Booking).
Replacing a venue does not change the event's own information or status.
A flagged arrangement is never changed or cancelled automatically.
A flagged venue booking or equipment reservation counts as outstanding and prevents confirmation until it is resolved (see: Track Outstanding Arrangements).
A Coordinator does not see flagged arrangements for events assigned to other Coordinators.

test_cases.title: The Flagged Arrangements page lists a flagged venue booking, equipment reservation and registrations on their own tabs, each with the event, the arrangement, why it was flagged and its current result, and leaves out the event's unflagged booking
test_cases.preconditions: The SPM-68 fixtures are loaded (npm run fixtures:spm68). 'SPM68 Listing Summit' is in Planning, assigned to Daniel Tan, on 7 Oct 2027, 09:00-17:00, for 50 people in Theatre layout. It has two approved venue bookings: SPM68 Hall (flagged for review) and SPM68 Annex (not flagged). Its reservation of 2 SPM68 Projector is flagged, and so are its registrations (12 registered, 3 on the waiting list). Logged in as Event Coordinator Daniel Tan (daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123). Nothing is changed in this case. Other stories' fixtures may add items to the same page; check only the items named here.
steps: Click 'SPM68 Listing Summit' in its item
test_cases.test_data:
Event: SPM68 Listing Summit (Planning), 7 Oct 2027, 09:00-17:00, 50 people, Theatre
Venue bookings: SPM68 Hall (Approved, flagged), SPM68 Annex (Approved, not flagged)
Equipment: SPM68 Projector x 2 (Reserved, flagged); 4 in stock
Registrations: 12 registered, 3 on the waiting list (flagged)
Coordinator: Daniel Tan
test_cases.expected_result:
Step 1: The 'Flagged Arrangements' page opens, with the link after 'Review Queue' in the sidebar. It has three tabs, 'Venue bookings', 'Equipment reservations' and 'Registrations', each followed by how many are flagged, and opens on 'Venue bookings'. There is an item for 'SPM68 Listing Summit' showing 'SPM68 Hall (SPM68-HAL)', '7 Oct 2027, 09:00–17:00', 'Theatre', 'Flagged because: the date or time changed; the venue requirements changed', 'Suitability: Suitable' and 'Availability: Available', with the buttons 'Keep booking', 'Find a replacement venue' and 'Open Venue tab'. There is no item for SPM68 Annex. No equipment or registrations are shown on this tab.
Step 2: The 'Equipment reservations' tab shows an item for 'SPM68 Listing Summit' with 'SPM68 Projector', 'Flagged because: the date or time changed' and 'Availability: 2 reserved, 4 available for these dates.', with the buttons 'Keep reservation' and 'Open Equipment tab'. No venue booking is shown on this tab.
Step 3: The 'Registrations' tab shows an item for 'SPM68 Listing Summit' with '12 registered, 3 on the waiting list' and 'Flagged because: the date or time changed', with the buttons 'Mark as reviewed' and 'Open Overview'.
Step 4: The 'SPM68 Listing Summit' item for SPM68 Hall is shown again.
Step 5: The event's Overview opens, with the status badge 'Planning'.
Step 6: Under 'Booking requests', both SPM68 Hall and SPM68 Annex are listed as 'Approved'.

open_questions: Written before the code (TDD, 2026-10-13); the code was built to these cases and the automated tests the same day. The cases have NOT yet been walked through the running app: npm run fixtures:spm68 has to be run first. Entries marked DECIDED were chosen here rather than taken from the story; change them in code and cases together.

RESOLVED 2026-10-13 (Kristen): the release half of AC12 was left out while Withdraw or Release Venue Booking (SPM-67) was not in main. SPM-67 merged to main on 2026-10-13 and this branch was updated from it the same day, so the release is now in scope: SPM-68-TC14 (release, after requesting the replacement).

RESOLVED 2026-10-13: the fixture script is written (scripts/seed-spm68.ts, npm run fixtures:spm68) with the same events and rooms appended to prisma/seed.ts. It creates, all titled 'SPM68 …' with seed keys 'spm68_…', organiser Rachel Ng, coordinator Daniel Tan unless said, status Planning, 09:00-17:00: five dedicated venues - SPM68 Hall (Theatre 100), Annex (60), Spare Room (200), Closed Room (60; unavailable for maintenance 9 Oct 2027 08:00-18:00) and Retired Room (60; retired), each with 'Fixed ceiling projector' and 'Step-free access'; two dedicated equipment items - SPM68 Projector (4 in stock) and SPM68 Speaker (2 in stock, 1 out of service); and 11 events - Listing Summit (7 Oct), Attendance Review (6 Oct), Outgrown Room (8 Oct), Venue Trouble Day (9 Oct), Moved Date (event 14 Oct, booking 13 Oct), Kit Recheck (15 Oct), Short Kit (16 Oct), Capacity Cut (17 Oct), Registration Off (18 Oct), Ready To Confirm (20 Oct) and Partner Briefing (21 Oct; Priya Raj). The flags are written directly; what the page shows for each is worked out live. It has not yet been run against the shared database.

RESOLVED 2026-10-13: AC2's 'venue setup or turnaround time changed' reason belongs to Re-check Bookings (SPM-80), which is not built, so nothing writes it and there is no case for it. The page shows a reason code it has not been taught in plain words rather than hiding the flag, so SPM-80's reason will appear without a change here; DOCUMENTATION.md's Known Gaps says where to add its wording.

AC9 says no registration is changed. No built screen lists an event's registrations (the Attendees tab is not built), so SPM-68-TC11 can only check that the registration settings are unchanged. That no registration row is written is covered by the automated route test.

SPM-68-TC12 relies on Confirm not waiting for the Operational Safety Check. When Resolve Safety Check Outcome (SPM-88) turns that gate on, the fixture event 'SPM68 Ready To Confirm' needs an approved safety check or the case will be refused for a different reason.

No manual case covers the empty page ('Nothing is flagged'): on the shared database every coordinator may have flagged arrangements from other stories' fixtures. It is covered by the automated page test.

DECIDED 2026-10-13, from the design not the story: the screen is a new page, 'Flagged Arrangements', at /flagged, with a 'Flagged Arrangements' link in the Event Coordinator's sidebar straight after 'Review Queue' (the next free screen number in UI_DESIGN.md is S-30). No other role has the link. It follows the Safety Checks page (SPM-85): a visitor who is not logged in is sent to log in and brought back (SPM-68-TC04); any other role sees 'You do not have access to this' with 'Reviewing flagged arrangements is the Event Coordinator's role. You can still see the events you are involved in from your Dashboard.' (SPM-68-TC03).

DECIDED 2026-10-13: the page layout and wording. Three tabs - 'Venue bookings', 'Equipment reservations', 'Registrations' - each followed by how many are flagged, with only the open tab's items on the page (changed 2026-10-13 from three stacked sections, at Kristen's request). A tab has its own address (/flagged?tab=venue, ?tab=equipment, ?tab=registrations). Opened from the sidebar the page shows the first tab that has something flagged; a tab with nothing reads 'No venue bookings are flagged', 'No equipment reservations are flagged' or 'No registrations are flagged'. Each item shows the event's title (a link to its Overview) and reference, the arrangement, and 'Flagged because: <reasons joined by ; >' in the same words the Readiness tab uses. Most recently flagged first. A venue item shows the venue as 'Name (CODE)', the booking's own date and times, its layout, 'Suitability: Suitable' or 'Not suitable' and 'Availability: Available' or 'Not available', each followed by what is unmet. An equipment item shows 'Availability: <n> reserved, <n> available for these dates.' ('<n> requested, …' for a request Technical Support have not reserved yet). A registrations item shows '<n> registered, <n> on the waiting list'. Buttons: 'Keep booking', 'Find a replacement venue', 'Keep reservation', 'Mark as reviewed'. When nothing is flagged: 'Nothing is flagged' with 'Arrangements appear here when a change to an event, a venue or equipment means they need another look.'

DECIDED 2026-10-13: what 'still meets the event's requirements' means for a venue booking (AC4, AC6, AC7). Suitability is the existing check (SPM-41) for the event's present attendance, layout and mandatory facilities - the session's attendance and layout for a session's booking. Availability is: the venue has not been retired; the booking's own times still cover the event's (or session's) present time, the rule a new request must pass (SPM-93); and nothing else holds or blocks the room for the booking's occupied time (the existing conflict check, SPM-44: an unavailable period, or another event's approved booking). Keep is refused unless both pass (SPM-68-TC06 to SPM-68-TC08).

DECIDED 2026-10-13: what 'still meets the event's requirements' means for an equipment reservation (AC5, AC6, AC7). The existing availability check (SPM-48) for the event's present dates, not counting this reservation's own units: a Reserved or Partially fulfilled line can be kept when the units available cover the quantity it has reserved; a line Technical Support have not reserved yet, when they cover the quantity requested (SPM-68-TC09, SPM-68-TC10).

DECIDED 2026-10-13: the messages. Kept: 'Flag cleared' with '<arrangement> for <event> was kept as it is.' Registrations reviewed: 'Flag cleared' with 'Registrations for <event> were marked as reviewed. No registration was changed.' Refused by the server: '<arrangement> no longer meets this event's requirements: <each unmet requirement>', shown inside the item, which stays listed - seen only when the page's result was out of date (see the decision on not offering Keep). The unmet venue requirements use the existing wording ('Theatre capacity is 100 - your event expects 150.', '<Venue> is unavailable at this time (maintenance, …).') plus two new ones: '<Venue> has been retired.' and 'The booking (<its times>) does not cover the event's time (<the event's times>).' Keeping asks for no confirmation: it changes nothing but the flag.

DECIDED 2026-10-13: keeping clears the flag and its reasons only. It does not change the event's status: a Confirmed event that Update Event Information (SPM-62) moved back to Planning stays in Planning until the Coordinator confirms it again. Which arrangements are listed: flagged venue bookings that are Pending or Approved, and flagged equipment lines that are Requested, Under review, Reserved or Partially fulfilled - a rejected or cancelled one holds nothing to review.

DECIDED 2026-10-13: the replacement search (AC11 to AC13). 'Find a replacement venue' opens the existing Find a venue page (SPM-40) for the event with the flagged booking named in the address. The form is filled from the booking's date, start and end times and layout, the attendance of the booking's session or the event, and the event's mandatory facilities and accessibility requirements; the page says 'Filled in from the flagged booking at <venue>. Change any filter and search again.' In that mode each result has a 'Request booking' button that opens the existing Request a venue booking form (SPM-42) for that venue. The request is an ordinary pending request; nothing about the flagged booking, the event's information or its status changes (SPM-68-TC13, SPM-68-TC13).

DECIDED 2026-10-13 (Kristen), replacing the decision of 2026-10-13: the Flagged Arrangements page has no 'Release booking' or 'Withdraw request' button. AC12 asks only that the flagged booking stays on the event record until the Coordinator releases it; releasing is Withdraw or Release Venue Booking (SPM-67), which is on the event's Venue tab, and a change to an event's bookings is made in that one place. The page clears flags and never changes an arrangement. Each flagged booking has an 'Open Venue tab' link to its event's Venue tab instead. A withdrawn or released booking holds nothing, so it leaves the page and stops blocking confirmation; its flag is not separately cleared (SPM-68-TC14).

RESOLVED 2026-10-13: every fixture date is in October 2027, not September. The app writes September as 'Sept' (8 Sept 2027), which is easy to mistype when checking a case against the screen; Withdraw or Release Venue Booking (SPM-67) moved its fixtures to November for the same reason.

DECIDED 2026-10-13, during the build: each venue booking and equipment item also shows its own status badge ('Approved', 'Pending', 'Reserved'), as the Venue and Equipment tabs do. A flagged booking that was later rejected, withdrawn or released, and an equipment line that was cancelled or could not be provided, is not listed. A replacement search opened for a booking that is no longer one of the event's bookings falls back to the ordinary search for that event.

RESOLVED 2026-10-13: reviewed against the built screen and for overlap, and cut from 17 cases to 15. Every remaining case still matches the screen. Two cases repeated another case's steps on the same event and were merged into it, with every check kept but one. (1) The case that an event with a flagged booking cannot be confirmed is now the opening of the keep case that followed it: the Readiness tab shows the booking as Outstanding before it is kept and Complete after. The check that was dropped is clicking 'Confirm event' to read the refusal message: that message is Track Outstanding Arrangements' and is already checked by SPM-33-TC05. (2) The case that the replacement search opens pre-filled was the first two steps of the case that requests the replacement, and is now part of it. The numbers of the later cases moved up to close the gaps.

RESOLVED 2026-10-13 (Kristen): the three kinds of flagged arrangement are tabs, not sections on one page. The cases that work on equipment or registrations now open that tab first (SPM-68-TC01, SPM-68-TC02, SPM-68-TC09 to SPM-68-TC12); the venue cases are unchanged because the page opens on 'Venue bookings' for Daniel Tan and Priya Raj, who both have a flagged venue booking in the fixtures.

RESOLVED 2026-10-13: with release and withdraw taken off the page, the case that withdrew a pending flagged request from it was removed (14 cases now) along with its fixture event 'SPM68 Pending Request'. Withdrawing a pending request on the Venue tab is SPM-67's (SPM-67-TC01), and a booking that is no longer pending or approved leaving this page is checked once, by the release in SPM-68-TC14, and by the automated route test. SPM-68-TC14 now reaches the Venue tab through 'Open Venue tab' and releases there.

DECIDED 2026-10-13 (Kristen), changing how AC7 is met: 'Keep booking' and 'Keep reservation' are offered only while the arrangement still meets the event's requirements. Where it does not, the item lists what is unmet, says 'This booking can't be kept while it doesn't meet the event's requirements.' ('This reservation …' for equipment) and has no Keep button - offering to keep a booking the page itself shows as clashing made no sense. AC7 is worded as 'when the Coordinator attempts to keep it': its outcome still holds (the flag is not cleared and the unmet requirement is identified), but the attempt cannot be made from the screen, so SPM-68-TC06, SPM-68-TC07, SPM-68-TC08 and SPM-68-TC10 check that Keep is absent rather than clicking it. The server still refuses a keep of an arrangement that no longer fits, for a page showing an older result; that refusal is covered by the automated tests only. Every equipment item also has 'Open Equipment tab', so one that cannot be kept is not a dead end.

DECIDED 2026-10-13 (Kristen): a registrations item also has 'Open Overview', a link to the event's Overview, where the Registration card's 'Change registration settings' (SPM-64) raises the capacity or turns registration back on. Like 'Open Venue tab' and 'Open Equipment tab', it only takes the Coordinator to where the change is made; the Flagged Arrangements page itself still changes nothing but the flag (SPM-68-TC01, SPM-68-TC11).
